metrics.name: follow_up_questions
metrics.title: Follow-up questions
metrics.evidence: Questions such as #2 (the cascade delete bug and whether anything beyond refactoring changed), #4 (quoting a specific CLAUDE.md claim about the parser and asking for a full explanation), #10 (whether a quoted sentence is proposed or existing), #13 (TrialRequest vs CriterionFilter request, eligibility, polarity), #26-28 (the schema file and package naming) and #31-33 (why the tests were added, whether they were moved, whether the python rules were applied) reference specific identifiers and decisions that only someone who had read the output could ask.

metrics.name: coding_guidelines
metrics.title: Coding guidelines
metrics.evidence: The general coding, git, python and project CLAUDE.md files were in context and most commit subjects follow the Angular form, but the JavaScript rule file and frontend/src/CLAUDE.md were never read despite a large frontend diff, and the subjects 'incorporate documents' and 'Update .gitignore' break the commit rules.

metrics.name: output_amendments
metrics.title: Output amendments
metrics.evidence: 30 of 4761 generated lines were rewritten after the author challenged them

metrics.name: prompt_granularity
metrics.title: Prompt granularity
metrics.evidence: Median generated lines per producing prompt was 24 (13 of 48 prompts produced output), well under the 50-line threshold, with prompts like 'y' and small scoped corrections approving incremental steps; only the 218-line plan-issue and a 178-line step exceeded 100.

metrics.name: generative_comments
metrics.title: Generative comments
metrics.evidence: 169 comment lines over 3511 lines of code, against a repository baseline of 0.014
